description: The reformed nationality law added three 'antisemitism filters', one inserted into section 10(1) sentence 1 StAG as number 1a, requiring applicants to affirm Germany's historical responsibility, peaceful coexistence of peoples, and the prohibition on the use of force in international law.
energy_note: A citizenship exam with a foreign policy question.

description: A stateless Palestinian, Sunni, who by his own account had never lived in Israel or Palestine but only in Syria, and was recognised as a refugee in Germany in 2016, was refused naturalisation for not recognising Israel. He argued his position was anti-Zionist rather than antisemitic. The court held that anti-Zionists cannot become Germans either - although the legislature had deliberately declined to require an explicit declaration on Israel.
energy_note: Refused a passport over a country he has never seen.

aspect: Deportation proposed without charge or conviction
description: The Berlin Senate sought to deport four pro-Palestinian activists over an occupation at the Free University while investigations were still running. None had been charged or convicted. Three were EU nationals and one American. Legal analysis considered the expulsions probably unlawful, not least under EU free movement.
energy_note: An expulsion order in advance of any charge.

aspect: There is precedent, and it is old
description: After the Black September attack at the 1972 Munich Olympics, many foreigners were expelled for membership of the General Union of Palestinian Students or Workers - association itself as the ground.
energy_note: Deported for belonging to a student union.

aspect: German-Palestinians get worse consular protection, by their own state's account
description: Berlin's immigration authority advises that the status derived from the Palestinian population registry is not a nationality in German law - but that Israel and the Palestinian authorities treat such Germans as dual nationals anyway, which can impede consular assistance.
energy_note: Your embassy may not be able to reach you.

aspect: Even the deportation destination is legally incoherent
description: The Lower Saxony higher administrative court held that naming 'Israel' as the destination state for a stateless Palestinian is defective - including with the addition 'West Bank', since the West Bank is not Israeli state territory. There is often no lawful country to deport the person to.
energy_note: Deportable in principle, to nowhere in particular.

aspect: So the safest strategy abroad is silence
description: Where naturalisation, residence and employment all carry a political test, the rational move is to say nothing about the place you are from, for the decade the process takes.
energy_note: Ten years of not mentioning where you're from.

aspect: EXAMPLE - Munich, 1972, and expulsion for membership
description: After the Black September attack at the 1972 Munich Olympics, West Germany expelled many foreigners for membership of the General Union of Palestinian Students or the General Union of Palestinian Workers. Association with a student body was itself the ground.
energy_note: Deported for being in a student union.
